definitions.explanation: The final day of any month. Originally meant the thirtieth day, but now refers to the last day regardless of how many days the month has.

examples.japanese: {三十日|みそか}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{支払|しはら}い⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I make payments on the last day of the month.

examples.japanese: ⟦{毎月|まいつき}→毎月：00732_maitsuki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{三十日|みそか}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{締|し}め{切|き}り→締め切り：04162_shimekiri⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There is a deadline on the last day of every month.

examples.japanese: ⟦{二月|にがつ}→二月：00657_nigatsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{三十日|みそか}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{二十八日|にじゅうはちにち}⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧{二十九日|にじゅうくにち}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: The last day of February falls on the 28th or 29th.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: {三十日|みそか} literally means the thirtieth day ({三十|みそ} is an old counting word for thirty + {日|か}, day). It has come to mean the last day of any month.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{大晦日|おおみそか}→大晦日：05810_oomisoka⟧: New Year's Eve (literally 'great last day') — the last day of the year, December 31st
- {晦日|みそか}: an alternate kanji spelling with the same meaning

USAGE: Less common in everyday speech than ⟦{月末|げつまつ}→月末：00070_getsumatsu⟧ (end of the month), but {三十日|みそか} has a traditional feel and is still used, especially in set phrases and financial contexts. The derived word ⟦{大晦日|おおみそか}→大晦日：05810_oomisoka⟧ is extremely common.
